syllabusTopics: Biotechnological applications in agriculture: Bt cotton, nematode-resistant tobacco
Biotechnological applications in medicine: insulin, gene therapy, therapeutic proteins
agentNotes: Authoring contract: frontend/AGENTS.md §9. Filled 2026-10-06 (Class 12 track); no Class-12 PYQ bank in-corpus, so the board row is NEB-style with no fabricated citation.

card.title: Bt crops to gene therapy — applied rDNA

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Agriculture: Bt cotton carries bacterial cry genes (bollworm guts perforate on feeding); nematode-resistant tobacco silences parasite genes via RNAi. Medicine: recombinant insulin (1983 — first therapeutic, E. coli-assembled A+B chains), gene therapy (ADA deficiency: patient lymphocytes corrected ex vivo), therapeutic proteins (tPA, interferons, growth hormone). Transgenic animals model disease and manufacture drugs (Rosie cow's enriched milk). Biopiracy (patenting others' bioresources — neem, turmeric, basmati fights) closes with ethics and patents.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: Bt: cryIAc/cryIIAb → gut-alkaline-activated toxin → pest death (plant-safe, human-safe)  ·  RNAi: dsRNA → Dicer → siRNA → RISC silences nematode mRNA  ·  insulin: proinsulin minus C-peptide, A+B chains + S–S bridges (E. coli)  ·  ADA therapy: lymphocyte harvest → corrected gene → reinfuse (not permanent — stem-cell fix needed)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Bt works on chewing pests ingesting toxin (sucking pests need other genes). RNAi needs sequence match to the target mRNA. Gene therapy needs ex-vivo cell survival + engraftment (lymphocytes die out — repeat doses). Patents need novelty + utility (traditional knowledge defeats biopiracy claims).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Golden rice (β-carotene pathway) fights vitamin-A blindness. Flavr Savr tomato delayed softening (antisense polygalacturonase). Dolly (cloned sheep) proved nuclear transfer; ANDi (fluorescent monkey) proved germline transgenesis. Bt resistance management mandates refuge (non-Bt) acres.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Why is recombinant insulin safer than pig insulin? Sequence-identical human protein (no allergy), unlimited fermenter supply (no slaughterhouse limits), no animal-pathogen risk. Production: synthesise A and B chain genes → express in E. coli → extract, join disulphides → purify — Eli Lilly's 1983 Humulin pipeline.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Gene therapy is mostly somatic and transient (germline edits raise heritable-ethics walls). Bt selects resistant pests (refuge strategy slows, not stops). Transgene escape via pollen worries ecologists. Biopiracy battles show patents lag behind traditional knowledge documentation.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: From tools to products: identify the gene (cry, insulin) → clone into a delivery vector (Ti plasmid for plants, retrovirus for ADA lymphocytes) → transform target → select expressers → scale (fields/fermenters/clinics). Each application reuses the principles-unit pipeline with a new cargo — the exam's favourite 'apply the pipeline' move.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Agri examples: Bt cotton (insect), RNAi tobacco (nematode), Golden rice (vitamin). Medicine: insulin (diabetes), ADA (gene therapy), tPA (clots). Ethics: biopiracy = patenting others' biodiversity (neem/turmeric/basmati defences).

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB-style: Bt mechanism with cry genes; nematode resistance via RNAi steps; insulin production pipeline; ADA gene-therapy procedure + limitation; biopiracy with one opposed patent.
